title: Mattawommax (Probable Fireplace Meadow)
summary: Mattawommax named a meadow locality in Brookhaven. Brookhaven's early town records place John Thompson's numbered meadow share in the 1664 Old Purchase at South, the landscape now associated with Brookhaven Hamlet, Bellport, and Fireplace Neck; the marker is a broad probable placement rather than an identified lot boundary.
address_label: Fireplace Neck, Brookhaven, NY (probable broad landscape)
map_geometry_source: Representative Fireplace Neck point based on Brookhaven town records placing John Thompson's meadow share in the Old Purchase at South; exact Mattawommax parcel unknown.
why_this_matters: Mattawommax preserves a Native name within the salt-meadow geography that drew Setauket proprietors to Brookhaven's south shore. Linking the deed to the Old Purchase at South makes the record visible while the probable label keeps a numbered colonial share from being mistaken for an exact recovered Native boundary.
introduction_content: Tooker cited a March 2, 1685 deed in which John Thompson transferred his share of meadow at Mattawommax to John Pallmer. The deed did not supply modern boundaries, but Brookhaven's town records identify Thompson as the holder of meadow lot 11 in the Old Purchase at South.
history_content: The 1664 purchase covered the south-shore landscape now including Brookhaven Hamlet, Bellport, and part of South Haven. The town divided salt meadow along the Great South Bay into numbered shares and later added nearby upland. This documentary connection narrows Mattawommax from the whole Town of Brookhaven to the Fireplace meadow landscape without recovering the exact historic parcel.
translation_content: Tooker interpreted Mattawommax as describing a place where travel or passage was difficult and connected that meaning with wet meadow ground. This is a historical linguistic interpretation, not a modern community-confirmed translation.
whereintheworld_content: The marker is a representative point on Fireplace Neck within the Old Purchase at South meadow landscape. It does not identify John Thompson's former lot line or prove that the name applied to this exact point.
